mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point or greater increase in the unemployment rate over the prior 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2% or greater decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the prior 6 months signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where RSAFS falls > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 1.5% or greater increase in the industrial production index over the prior 3 months signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where INDPRO rises > 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate and a decline of at least 0.5% in average hourly earnings over the prior 3 months signals a dual labor market shock, which reduces both consumer demand and corporate pricing power, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND HOUST falls > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where both UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and HOUST falls > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% combined with a consumer price index increase above 3% over the prior 12 months signals a restrictive monetary regime, which reduces borrowing and spending, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL rises > 3% in 12 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where both FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL rises > 3% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 5% or greater decline in the housing starts index over the prior 6 months signals a collapse in residential investment, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where HOUST falls > 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 1% or greater increase in real personal consumption expenditures over the prior 3 months signals strengthening household demand, which boosts revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where RSAFS rises > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).
